content: 1. Intranasal administration of isoniazid can increase the levels or effects of diazepam by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of diazepam intranasally by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Strong or moderate inhibitors of CYP3A4 may reduce the elimination rate of diazepam, leading to an increased risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Isoniazid and dichlorphenamide can synergistically increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic interactions. Both drugs are capable of causing metabolic acidosis. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 5. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache should be monitored. 6. Both dihydroergotamine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 7. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 8. Disulfiram increases the levels or effects of isoniazid by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2E1. Isoniazid, in turn, increases the toxicity of disulfiram by reducing its metabolism. Enhanced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity may occur. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of doravirine by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 11. Both doxepin and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 12. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and doxorubicin liposomal by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Both duloxetine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of elagolix by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. The elagolix dose should be limited to 150 mg daily, and the duration of CYP3A inhibitor use should not exceed six months. 18. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both eletriptan and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Isoniazid increases the levels of eluxadoline by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 20. Isoniazid increases the levels of elvitegravir by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Elvitegravir is a substrate of CYP3A4, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate its levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Isoniazid increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase free MMAE exposure, potentially elevating the incidence or severity of toxicities. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 23. Both ergotamine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Both escitalopram and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations of estrogens and their toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ethanol by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2E1. Generally, this combination should be avoided due to an increased risk of hepatotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Ethionamide increases the levels of isoniazid through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of etravirine by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Both fenfluramine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of finasteride by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of finerenone by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 37. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Co-administration with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors may elevate flibanserin exposure, increasing the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 38. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Both fluoxetine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate and fluticasone inhaled by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Both fluvoxamine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Both frovatriptan and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Isoniazid increases the levels of gefitinib by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of gepirone by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both gepirone and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor for symptoms of serotonin syndrome when gepirone is used with other serotonergic drugs. If serotonin syndrome occurs, consider discontinuing gepirone and/or the concomitant serotonergic drug. 47. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Green tea and isoniazid may interact. Avoid excessive consumption of green tea, as the caffeine component may increase the risk of cardiac arrhythmias or severe hypertension. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 50. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 52. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 53. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of imipramine by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Both imipramine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 57. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 58. Isoniazid decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Rarely, isoniazid may increase blood glucose levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Isoniazid decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Rarely, isoniazid may increase blood glucose levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Isoniazid decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Rarely, isoniazid may increase blood glucose levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Isoniazid decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 62. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of isradipine by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 63. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Isoniazid decreases the levels of itraconazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 65. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 66. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 67. Both isoniazid and L-tryptophan increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 68. Isoniazid increases the levels of lacosamide by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 69. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 70. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 71. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may necessitate dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 72. Isoniazid decreases the effects of inhaled levodopa by altering its metabolism. Isoniazid may inhibit dopa-decarboxylase in the brain, thereby preventing the conversion of levodopa to active dopamine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 73. Both levomilnacipran and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Isoniazid also increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 74. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma hormone concentrations. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. Caution and monitoring are advised. 75. Both isoniazid and lithium increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 76. Both lofepramine and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 77. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 78. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of loratadine by altering the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. 79. Both isoniazid and LSD increase serotonin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 80. Isoniazid increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
